components.title: Crest gate
components.description: A movable steel barrier. Lowering it allows excess water out when sea level permits.

stops.title: A park that manages water
stops.body: A public roof sits beside working water infrastructure. Find the reservoir, the sea, nine gate bays and the pump hall. The overall scene compresses distance to make their relationships readable.

stops.title: Why build here?
stops.body: The vision depended on cleaner waterways and improving treatment technology. Follow the urban catchment on the map: a reservoir captures rain, but that water still needs treatment before drinking.

stops.title: Building in water
stops.body: A temporary enclosure makes a dry working area possible. Scrub to remove water and expose the illustrative work floor. The work sequence and dimensions are conceptual, not the contractor’s historical programme.

stops.title: Putting it together
stops.body: Reveal the supporting structure, place equipment and complete the crossing. This sequence explains interfaces; it does not establish the actual order or duration of each construction package.

stops.title: Rain at low tide
stops.body: When the reservoir can drain towards the lower sea, crest gates lower to release excess water. Compare the two water levels and follow the arrows. The gate does not lift vertically like a sluice.

stops.title: Rain at high tide
stops.body: High sea level prevents the low-tide release mode. The tidal barrier stays closed while drainage pumps move excess rainwater out. The enlarged pump section is displaced beside the gate for teaching; its internal shape is illustrative.

stops.title: Becoming freshwater
stops.body: Opening the Barrage and commissioning a freshwater reservoir were different milestones. Rain gradually replaced saline water; this was not a desalination plant installed in the gate.

stops.title: Keeping it dependable
stops.body: Weather, reservoir level and tide inform operation. There is no fixed gate-opening timetable. Equipment inspection and availability matter; this exhibit does not reproduce PUB operating thresholds or isolation procedures.

stops.title: Facing future seas
stops.body: PUB announced a future retrofit in 2025. Compare the current barrier with an optional, ghosted gap-treatment concept. This is not a completed upgrade or a promised 2050 delivery date.
